fields.title: 📖 When the intermediary is made someone to call upon
fields.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** said:

> ***“Whoever makes the angels and the prophets intermediaries, calls upon them, places his trust in them and asks them to bring benefit and to turn away harm … he is a Kāfir by the consensus of the Muslims.”***

What is meant is not the permitted asking of a living person for Duʿāʾ, or for help in what he is able to do. What is meant is calling upon someone besides **Allah**, placing tawakkul upon him and asking him for things that only **Allah** can do.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever attributes to prophets or angels what belongs to Allah alone leaves the core of **Tawḥīd**. Duʿāʾ, trust and rescue from distress belong to **Allah alone**.

immutable.source: 📝 Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā, Bd. 1, S. 124; vgl. al-Fatāwā al-Kubrā, Bd. 4, S. 606.
